kid.en: How warm the air is just above the ground.

student.en: Monthly average air temperature 2 metres above the ground, in degrees Celsius.

scientist.en: 2 m air temperature (T2M) from the MERRA-2 reanalysis, monthly mean.

caveats: MERRA-2 is a model reanalysis, not a direct measurement.
Each grid cell is about 50 km wide, so a city and its surroundings share one value.

kid.en: How much rain falls from the sky.

student.en: Total rain reaching the ground in a month, in millimetres.

scientist.en: Satellite-gauge merged monthly precipitation from GPM IMERG Final Run.

qa.convert: mm/hr -> mm/month (x hours in month), check units on download

caveats: Record starts in mid-2000, so about 25 years.
Algorithm version changes can shift values.

kid.en: How green and leafy the plants are, seen from space.

student.en: A greenness score measured from space, usually between 0 and 1; higher means more green, healthy leaves. It is called EVI, the Enhanced Vegetation Index.

scientist.en: Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) from MODIS Terra MOD13A3 version 061, layer _1_km_monthly_EVI, as the monthly area mean from a NASA AppEEARS area-statistics export. Like NDVI it compares near-infrared and red reflectance, but it also uses the blue band to reduce haze and soil-background effects, so it keeps responding over dense canopy.

caveats: January values are missing from the AppEEARS export, so each year has at most 11 months.
Clouds can contaminate monthly values in the rainy season.
EVI is less prone than NDVI to saturating over dense forest, so it shows change there better, but it is a different index and its values are not NDVI values.
